title: Coefficient-linear normalized comparison at scalar levels
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ have topology $J$, let $U\in\mathcal C$, let $O$ be a commutative ring sheaf, let $B:\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(J,\mathrm{CommRing})$ and let $\alpha:\operatorname{const}O\to B$. Assume module sheafification on $J$ and $J/U$ in a common coefficient universe with its locally bijective characterization. Fix any presentations $A_X,A_U,E$ satisfying [def-sf-semilinear-slice-scalar-data]. There is a SliceScalarLevelComparison: for every $O|_U$-module sheaf $G$ and level $n$, a $B_n$-linear isomorphism $B_n\otimes_O j_{O!}G\cong j_{B_n!}(B_n|_U\otimes_{O|_U}G)$, whose hom sends $b\otimes[x]_f$ to $[b|_f\otimes x]_f$ and is the unique morphism with that formula. For every $B_n|_U$-module sheaf $F$ there is an $O$-linear identification $j_{O!}(\operatorname{Res}F)\cong\operatorname{Res}(j_{B_n!}F)$ preserving every original summand and uniquely so normalized. After the prescribed object transports, the forward level maps commute with every coefficient transition and are natural in $G$. This asserts levelwise maps and equations only; it does not construct the presentations, a strict-system inverse, an augmentation identity or a complex lift.

proof.text: Apply the proved generic scalar/slice adjunction comparison to each alpha_n and G, obtaining the coefficient-linear isomorphism with its full pure-generator formula. The generic Hom extensionality theorem detects maps on unit tensors in original summands. Apply it and the generator formula at coefficient 1 to prove uniqueness. No ordinary tensor comparison, local representatives or coefficient-linearity extension argument remains in the tower module.

proof.text: Apply the already proved identity-induced scalar/slice-extension comparison to alpha_n. Its inverse gives scalarIdentification in the required direction. Its forward generator equation and its inverse identity prove the inverse generator equation. The normalized slice-extension Hom equivalence proves that any two O-linear maps agreeing on every original summand are equal; apply this to obtain scalarIdentification_unique.

proof.text: Cancel the source and target object transports in each coherence equation and test equality with the injective composite Hom equivalence from step 2. The presentation transition_pure equations for AX and AV, and extension.transition_generator, make both transition composites send 1 tensor [x]_f to the summand containing the corresponding unit tensor at the lower level. For naturality, map_eq for AX, AV and extension, naturality of the sheafification unit, and naturality of the normalized slice-extension unit make both sides send the same generator to the summand containing 1 tensor g(x). The inverse object transports cancel by eqToHom composition. No flatness or global generation is used.
